top.title: Jemimah Rodrigues to lead Mumbai in Super League stage of Senior Women's T20 Trophy
top.description: MUMBAI : India women's team batter Jemimah Rodrigues will lead Mumbai in the upcoming Super League stage of the Senior Women's T20 Trophy. The Super League will be played in Ahmedabad from November 14. Rodrigues had smashed 107 off just 47 balls against Pondicherry in their sixth and last match of the league stage of the Senior Women's T20 in Pune on Friday to star in Mumbai's 83-run victory. Rodrigues' century took Mumbai to the Super League stage of the tournament. Returning from a four-month layoff from the game due to a hamstring injury, Rodrigues had scored 58 off 41 balls against Delhi and 26 not out off 19 balls against Uttar Pradesh in a nine-over game. "Jemi's century yesterday was quite good, because the ball wasn't coming nicely on the bat. There was low bounce, it wasn't a flat pitch, but she placed the ball well, piercing the gap between two fielders, instead of trying to hit the ball hard. She played very smartly; it was a smartly built innings, as, realising the nature of the wicket, she didn't want to go for big shots. She came to bat in the fifth over of the innings and started off with two paddle sweeps, which got her two twos, and then gave us the necessary momentum. She paced her knock well and got to her century in the last over," Mumbai Women's team head coach Ajay Kadam told TOI. Interestingly, despite being the Delhi Capitals captain, Rodrigues wasn't the Mumbai skipper in the league stage of the tournament, as she joined the team late. Mumbai were captained by Manali Dakshini. "Jemimah was fine with that. She has no issues with that. She's a team player," Kadam said. Praising the impact of Rodrigues on the team, Kadam said, "Jemimah has definitely added a lot of energy to our dressing room. She has gained vast experience by now. Her presence matters a lot. The girls look up to her. She joined the team after a few matches, but since then, has played her role very well. She has lifted the team to a whole new level, given them confidence. She is a star."

top.title: Tee Higgins makes his 50th career touchdown catch
top.description: Cincinnati Bengals receiver Tee Higgins recorded his 50th career touchdown catch during the second quarter of an NFL Week 9 game against the Atlanta Falcons at Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain. Higgins scored on a 4-yard pass from quarterback Joe Burrow . Higgins' 50th career TD reception was his fifth of this season. He's in his seventh NFL season, all with the Bengals. "It's just not fair," NFL Network analyst Louis Riddick said during the broadcast. "It's just not fair. Watch how Tee Higgins catches this ball." Higgins entered the game ranked second in the NFL in receiving yardage this season, trailing only the Seattle Seahawks ' Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Higgins was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week for his effort in Cincinnati's 43-36 overtime win in NFL Week 8 against Tennessee. It was Higgins' first-ever AFC Offensive Player of the Week award. Higgins had 10 catches for 155 receiving yards against the Titans, and caught two of quarterback Joe Burrow's five touchdown passes . After being held without a catch during the first half, Higgins went off during the second half of a Week 7 rout in Baltimore, catching six Joe Burrow passes for 148 receiving yards with a touchdown. Earlier in the second half, Higgins' shoulder and arm were evaluated by medical personnel after he absorbed a big hit from Ravens defensive back Kyle Hamilton after a catch. Before the bye week, Higgins was dealing with an adductor injury he suffered in a Week 4 loss to Jacksonville. top.description: Ridle Baku called up to Germany squad Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp has given RBL defender Ridle Baku a late call-up ahead of the Nations League games against Serbia and the Netherlands . The 28-year-old joins teammate Brajan Gruda as the two RBL representatives in the 24-man squad. Klopp had praised Baku for his goal against Manchester City during the official squad announcement on Thursday, 5th November, and had mentioned that he was keeping the defender in mind as a replacement call-up. Baku has now been included in the squad following the news that Waldemar Anton would not be able to take part in the upcoming matches due to muscle problems. Aiming for his tenth Germany cap Baku will travel to the adidas Home Ground in Herzogenaurach with the team on Monday. The defender had been part of the squad in October for the Nations League matches against Serbia and Greece, but did not feature in either. Baku has been capped eight times at senior level for Germany, scoring twice in the process. So far this season, Baku has had a hand in four goals for RBL in 13 competitive games (3 goals, 1 assist) . top.title: Igor Thiago's moment of madness - Brentford striker sees red against Brighton after VAR review
top.description: Brighton & Hove Albion v Brentford - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Brentford striker Igor Thiago endured a disastrous afternoon at the Amex Stadium after being sent off for a moment of madness against Brighton. The Bees forward was dismissed for violent conduct, leaving his teammates with a mountain to climb in the Premier League encounter. Disciplinary disaster for Brentford star The Bees' hopes of securing a positive result against Brighton were dealt a massive blow early in the first half when Thiago was brandished a straight red card. Following a heated exchange on the pitch, the striker appeared to lose his composure and pushed Seagulls midfielder Chema Andres in the face. The incident initially escaped the on-field official's full attention, but the technology quickly intervened to ensure the correct disciplinary action was taken. Brighton capitalise on numerical advantage The red card only compounded the misery for Brentford, who were already trailing in the contest before the sending off occurred. Diego Gomez had given Brighton the lead after just fifteen minutes, finishing off a slick move that highlighted the gulf in confidence between the two sides. To make matters worse right on the stroke of half-time, the ever-reliable Pascal Gross converted a penalty to leave the Bees facing an insurmountable task. Brighton took full advantage of the extra space on the pitch, dominating possession and looking to secure their position in the upper echelons of the Premier League table. Fabian Hurzeler's side entered the match with the knowledge that a victory would propel them into second place, providing a major boost ahead of the impending international break. Thiago ban adds to Brentford's fixture nightmare The timing of Thiago's dismissal creates a major headache for Brentford given their daunting upcoming schedule. Following the international break, the Bees host Everton and travel to Manchester United, before facing a brutal start to December with back-to-back fixtures against title contenders Arsenal and Manchester City. With the forward facing a potential three-match ban for violent conduct, he is set to miss crucial games as Keith Andrews' side look to navigate a challenging run. Season stats so far Thiago joined Brentford in the summer of 2024 from Belgian side Club Brugge. This season, the forward has made 13 appearances across all competitions, scoring four goals and providing two assists.

top.title: Superstitions prevail: If it ain’t broke, don’t move
top.description: As Erick Fedde and Kyle Teel celebrated the White Sox clinching the AL Wild Card series, fans could take a breath and relax following a day of superstitious rituals. | (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) I didn’t move. Not when Sam Antonacci doubled to open the second game of the American League Wild Card series against the Houston Astros. Not when Kyle Teel singled him home. And certainly not when Andrew Benintendi delivered a two-run single that helped the Chicago White Sox build a four-run lead before the Astros could record their second out. There I sat, practically frozen in place, convinced that the slightest movement might somehow bring Chicago’s offensive outburst to an abrupt end. Never mind that I was hundreds of miles from Daikin Park in Houston. Never mind that the White Sox players had absolutely no idea who I was, what I was wearing or whether I had gotten up to use the bathroom. And never mind that my position on the couch had precisely zero influence on a baseball traveling toward home plate at nearly 100 mph. The White Sox were scoring. I wasn’t moving. It wasn’t until Tristan Peters singled home Chicago’s fourth run and the inning finally ended that I allowed myself to get comfortable again. Welcome to the wonderfully irrational world of sports superstitions, where otherwise reasonable adults become convinced that a lucky jersey, a particular snack or the precise arrangement of living room furniture might determine whether their favorite team wins or loses. And apparently, I’m not alone. A little luck never hurt anyone My postseason wardrobe consisted of White Sox jerseys. Every game. No exceptions. When football season arrives, the situation becomes considerably more complicated. I pay attention to whether my team (either the Chicago Bears or Jacksonville Jaguars) is playing at home or on the road, choosing my jersey accordingly. I try to eat the same foods, snack at the same times and sit in the same location. It’s definitely easy for my wife. Honestly, she probably thinks it’s a little obnoxious. Sometimes a particular shirt becomes lucky. Other times, a hat gets blamed for a loss. I understand how ridiculous this sounds. I also know that if the White Sox had continued scoring every time I remained motionless during the playoffs, there’s a good chance someone would have needed to bring me dinner. But the impulse to create rituals around sporting events isn’t unusual. A 2018 study published in Sport Management Review examined how superstitions influence the experience of watching sports. Researchers found that these behaviors were associated with fans’ emotional states during games and that more superstitious fans were more likely to attribute outcomes to outside influences such as fate or officiating. In other words, fans aren’t necessarily trying to control a baseball game. They’re trying to control how helpless they feel while watching one. top.title: Previous Infantino ally Wenger considering FIFA presidency bid
top.description: FILE PHOTO - FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development Arsène Wenger stands in the stadium prior to the start of the UEFA Champions League final soccer match between Borussia Dortmund and Real Madrid at Wembley Stadium. (is associated with: «Previous Infantino ally Wenger considering FIFA presidency bid») Robert Michael/dpa Arsène Wenger is considering whether to put himself forward as a candidate for the FIFA presidency, the Press Association understands. The former Arsenal manager, 77, remains in the mix as one of a number of candidates UEFA could give its backing to as it seeks to put up a credible alternative to incumbent Gianni Infantino. However, Wenger is not yet seen as the preferred candidate, with others still being evaluated as well. It is understood he is still undecided over whether to run. Wenger’s reputation within football and close knowledge of the FIFA administration would make him a formidable opponent for Infantino if he did choose to go for it, with the Frenchman having served as FIFA’s chief of global football development since 2019. UEFA is expected to hold meetings of its executive committee as well as gather together its member national associations this coming week to hold further discussions on who should get Europe’s support. Infantino’s position appeared under threat when his plans to sell a minority stake in a World Cup company, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), to private investors came to light. The plan was rejected by three continental confederations, including UEFA, and even though Infantino later abandoned it, the European body said it had “lost confidence” in the Swiss and has since been working to identify someone to run against him. Wenger spoke out about the FFE plan on August 4, saying he was “not involved” in it and first became aware of it through media reports. He added: “The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent FIFA that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity.” Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association (JFA), announced on Thursday he would run for the presidency. Infantino has recovered and has rallied support from Africa, Asia, Oceania and South America. On Friday, he also received the backing of the member nations of the Caribbean Football Union (CFU). The election for the next FIFA president will take place at the FIFA Congress in Rabat, Morocco on March 18 next year.

top.description: KNOXVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 07: Mike Bethea II #55, Ian Duarte #81, and Dejuan Lane #10 celebrate after a 34-6 victory against the Kentucky Wildcats at Neyland Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Knoxville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Vols pulled off one of the more impressive performances of the college football season for the second time in less than a month, clubbing No. 6 Kentucky 34-6 on Saturday night at Neyland Stadium. Tennessee, of course, also handled Alabama at home three weeks ago 26-10 in a win that’s shaping up as one of the best across the country in early November. Of course, Tennessee wasn’t really credited with that win the way that some felt they should in the initial college football rankings, coming in at No. 13. But the Vols will surely find themselves in the field at this point after winning handily over their border rival. Ole Miss, Ohio State, and BYU were all ahead of Tennessee. All should drop below the Vols, who were two spots out of the bracket at this point (yes, it’s early. Don’t need to be reminded of that.) So where does Tennessee sit in the latest projections from ESPN’s Heather Dinich ? At No. 9, one spot ahead of Kentucky. Why they could be here: The Vols moved up because Ole Miss and Ohio State suffered third losses, but also because of Saturday’s statement win against Kentucky and the Oct. 17 win against Alabama. The head-to-head win against Kentucky will keep the Vols above the Wildcats, but the committee made it clear in its first ranking that it thought the gap between Alabama and Tennessee was wide enough to outweigh the Vols’ 16-point win last month. Dinich is right even if it’s ridiculous regarding the gap between Tennessee and Alabama. Alabama throttled LSU 31-13 and will move up again in the rankings this week from No. 5. Tennessee won’t be in the same grouping as Alabama, which committee chair Hunter Yuracheck has said is why the Vols’ head-to-head win/advantage over the Crimson Tide isn’t being honored. That seems pretty clear to me, and that’s something Dinich said, too. Need to know: Head-to-head results are one factor, but they’re not the determining difference in the room — especially if the committee doesn’t deem the teams comparable. “That head-to-head matchup where South Carolina beat Tennessee is not going to come into play,” Yurachek said, “just like the head-to-head matchup between Tennessee and Alabama is not going to come into play at this point because of where those teams were reviewed in the ranking process.” Of course, the task now turns to Texas A&M, which, to me, is more worrisome than Kentucky. Yes, really. That’s a tougher road trip than the record might indicate. I do like the chances of Tennessee’s defense to outduel Marcel Reed and the A&M offense. But I still worry about this game. top.title: Georgia reacts to after stomping Ole Miss football
top.description: The Georgia Bulldogs took it on the road this week to take on the Ole Miss Rebels and the Bulldogs had one thing on their minds and that was to win. Well, they did just that in a very big way. Georgia went into Oxford and dominated the Rebels by a 42-7 score. One big takeaway is how the Bulldogs defense has played since coming back from their bye week. They have flat out shut down the last two opponents and holding both Florida and Ole Miss under 10 points. Georgia's defense played lights out for the second week in a row and being able to do that against a game changing quarterback like Trinidad Chambliss is simply impressive. The Georgia offense took their game a couple of notches up and they didn't hold back against the Rebels. The Bulldogs racked up 481 total yards of offense against Ole Miss. Georgia rushed for 295 yards on 48 carries. Through the air, the Bulldogs passed for 186. Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton was 9-of-15 for 186, four touchdowns, 22 rushing yards and a touchdown on the ground. Bulldogs wide receiver. Talan Taylor had four receptions, 140 yards and 3 touchdowns. Bulldogs running back Nate Frazier had over 100 rushing on the night. Georgia reacts to win over Ole Miss Kirby Smart reacts to Bulldogs' defensive staff "I'm really proud of the whole defensive staff. Glenn (Schumann) does a great job...Our kids stuck to the plan. The plan was to possess the ball offensively, own the line of scrimmage, we did that in the first half and stay aggressive on defense." Smart stated. The defensive staff did a tremendous job in back-to-back weeks when it comes to putting their defensive players in the best position possible to be successful. Because of the preparation from the Georgia defensive staff, Georgia's defensive unit caused havoc all night in Oxford. Gunner Stockton reacts to fast offensive start "It's a good feeling getting momentum early. We just try to stay on schedule and execute the plan...having that momentum makes a big difference." Gunner said. The Bulldogs took criticism from some fans after last weeks offensive performance against the Florida Gators for not putting a ton of points on the board and moving the ball at a better rate. However, the Bulldogs defense made up for any lack of offense. This week against Ole Miss was much different as Georgia came out scoring quickly and often. The Bulldogs did not let up and made an all-around statement to the country on how good they can be when they execute at a high level in all facets of the game. The Bulldogs will turn the page and look to continue it's momentum against the Missouri Tigers next week in Athens. top.title: Bayern Munich’s Uli Hoeneß worried about future with Jamal Musiala
top.description: (Photo by N. Hermann/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images Jamal Musiala’s recovery from a muscular injury has taken longer than many expected, which can happen with injuries of that type. However, in an interview with BR24 via t-online (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), Uli Hoeneß has offered a sobering assessment of the Bayern Munich star’s overall situation, including hi s neurological condition. The club’s honorary president spoke about Musiala’s condition, revealin g that the 23-year-old is dealing with a condition that cannot simply be cured and raising doubts about whether he will ever return to his previous level of performance. Hoeneß made a point of distinguishing Musiala’s situation from Vincent Kom pany’s recent health problems, suggesting that Bayern Munich is facing a much more complicated dilemma with its young playmaker. “With Musiala, the situation is completely different [to Vincent Kompany]. He expanded on the difficu lt position this creates for the club: “We’re in a dilemma with him. He has an illness that cannot simply be cured, bu t can be managed to some extent with medication. nigeria.title: Tinubu to inaugurate Kaduna-Kano rail Dec 3, says APC-PCC
nigeria.description: Orders immediate settlement of land compensation By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has said President Bola Tinubu will inaugurate the Kaduna-Kano Standard Gauge Railway on December 3, 2026, and has ordered that all outstanding land acquisition and compensation issues in Kaduna metropolis be settled immediately. The directive is meant to clear the way for the completion of the railway corridor from Abuja to Kano. Council spokesman, Dele Alake, in a statement on Sunday in Abuja said the President “is accelerating the completion of major railway projects in Northern Nigeria.” According to Alake, the President “has also directed that all outstanding land acquisition and compensation issues within Kaduna metropolis should be resolved immediately so that the railway corridor from Abuja to Kano will be completed.” The statement specifically said the “completed 190-kilometre Jaji-Kano section” of the Kaduna-Kano project and the “250-kilometre Dawanu-Kano-Kazaure-Daura-Katsina section of the Kano-Maradi project will be inaugurated by December 3, 2026.” Alake said the Kaduna-Kano line has reached “approximately 90 percent completion,” while the 400-kilometre Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway “has attained 70 percent completion.” He said both projects were far behind when the President took office. “When President Tinubu assumed office in 2023, Kano-Katsina-Maradi rail project was at barely 5% while Kaduna-Kano was less than 30% completion,” the statement said. The Kaduna-Kano line is an extension of the existing Abuja-Kaduna standard gauge line. It “will establish a continuous rail connection between Abuja, Kaduna, Zaria and Kano,” the statement said. The statement said a Federal Government team recently inspected the two projects on the President’s directive. The team was led by the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Transportation, Engr. Funso Adebiyi. Adebiyi “expressed satisfaction with the quality of construction work, particularly the railway alignment, drainage infrastructure, embankment protection, stone pitching and soil stabilisation,” the statement said. It added that the inspection “included a train test-run journey from Jaji in Kaduna State to Kano, allowing officials to assess the completed track infrastructure and passenger comfort.” On what the lines will deliver, Alake said the Kaduna-Kano railway, when operational, “will improve passenger transportation, facilitate commercial activities and provide an alternative to road travel along one of Northern Nigeria’s busiest commercial corridors.” He said the Kano-Katsina-Maradi railway “is expected to strengthen cross-border transportation and trade between Nigeria and the neighbouring Niger Republic.” “In line with President Tinubu’s agenda, all ongoing infrastructure projects will be delivered in every part of the country as scheduled,” Alake said. Busari in a post-match interview, said the performance of African teams at the tournament reflected growing quality, character and competitiveness, despite the challenges posed by strong opposition. The coach also expressed hope that more African teams would progress beyond the knockout stages in future editions of the competition and eventually reach the final. Reflecting on the Flamingos’ encounter with Japan, Busari explained that his technical crew had identified the Japanese team’s strength in winning second balls and exploiting spaces behind defensive lines. ﻿ He said the team adjusted its approach to limit Japan’s attacking opportunities, particularly by directing long balls into spaces rather than areas where the opposition could easily gain possession. Busari explained that the Flamingos initially sought to score early before adopting a more cautious approach after taking the lead, but Japan eventually found an equaliser through a set-piece situation. The series will end with a presidential debate/townhall. ﻿ The Lagos debate will hold at 7:00 p.m. at The Hub by IALA, House of His Glory, Plot 18, Providence Road, beside Keystone Bank, Marwa, Lekki, Lagos State. The major contenders for the Lagos governorship seat include incumbent Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), and Funso Doherty of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC). The organisers had earlier explained that the initiative would provide a credible, non-partisan platform for participating candidates to present their agendas, defend their policy choices and respond to questions on the issues that matter most to Lagos residents. It will provide an opportunity for voters to put the candidates’ capacity, ideas and priorities — from transportation and infrastructure to security, housing, education, healthcare, job creation and economic growth — under public scrutiny before the February 6, 2027, governorship elections. The Consortium assured that the debate would adhere to established professional standards, with fairness, neutrality, equal opportunity and editorial independence as guiding principles. It added that all participating candidates would be subject to the same rules, speaking times and moderation standards. nigeria.title: UK lists 4 conditions migrants must meet to qualify for permanent residency
nigeria.description: The United Kingdom, UK has introduced four mandatory conditions migrants must satisfy to qualify for permanent residency under its proposed earned settlement model, which will make obtaining indefinite leave to remain (ILR) dependent on applicants’ contributions and conduct. Under the proposed reforms, migrants will no longer qualify for permanent residency almost automatically after five years in the country. Instead, the time required to secure settled status will depend on their earnings, contribution to society and immigration history. The four non-negotiable conditions, which will apply to all applicants regardless of when they arrived in the UK, include: 1. Clean criminal record: Migrants must have a spotless criminal record, with the government proposing stricter requirements than the current rules, which allow some applicants with suspended sentences of up to 12 months to qualify. 2. High English proficiency: Applicants must demonstrate a high standard of spoken English, equivalent to A-Level English as a foreign language. 3. No outstanding government debts: Migrants must have cleared any debts owed to the UK government or taxpayer before qualifying for permanent residency. 4. Sustained National Insurance contributions: Applicants must provide evidence of sustained National Insurance contributions as proof of their economic contribution to the country. Beyond these four mandatory requirements, the proposed model introduces different settlement timelines based on migrants’ earnings and contributions. Under the arrangement, the highest earners could qualify for permanent residency after three years, while migrants earning more than £50,271 annually could become eligible after five years. Certain public service workers, including doctors, nurses and teachers, would also qualify for settlement after five years. Other migrants would be subject to a new standard settlement period of 10 years, while those who have breached immigration rules would have to wait at least 20 years before qualifying. The government said the reforms recognise settled status as a significant privilege, granting migrants unrestricted access to the labour market, the National Health Service (NHS) and the welfare system. The proposed changes are intended to make permanent residency a status migrants must earn rather than an entitlement granted after a fixed period. nigeria.title: Bandits kill 12 family members, abduct others in Zamfara
nigeria.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Armed men suspected to be bandits have killed 12 members of the same family and abducted several residents during an attack on Gidan Taba village in Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State. The attack reportedly occurred on Saturday night in Dosara Birnin Kaya Ward, with the assailants setting a room ablaze after the family members reportedly locked themselves inside to avoid being abducted. A source in the area told Vanguard that the victims belonged to the family of one Mallam Muhammadu Sani, who had gathered his relatives in a single room in an attempt to protect them from the attackers. According to the source, the bandits ordered the occupants to open the door but, after they refused, set fire around the room, killing all 12 family members. The 12 victims were buried on Sunday morning in accordance with Islamic rites. The attack comes amid recurring bandit attacks and security concerns along the busy Gusau-Sokoto road, where commuters have continued to face threats from armed criminals. nigeria.title: Court awards N50m damages against Pararan over defamation
nigeria.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi EFFURUN — A Delta State High Court sitting in Effurun, Uvwie Local Government Area, has awarded N50 million in damages against the proprietor of Pararan Mock News, Diamond Dietanuru Osakorigho, popularly known as Pararan, over a Facebook publication found to be defamatory against Apostle Michael Akpor. The court, presided over by Justice R.D. Harriman, also ordered Osakorigho to publish an unreserved apology to the cleric in Vanguard and The Nation newspapers within 14 days. It directed that the apology must enjoy the same prominence and circulation as the original publication. The judgment was delivered on November 6, 2026, in Suit No. EHC/91/2023. The court further restrained the defendant, his agents, privies, servants and all persons acting through him from publishing or causing to be published any further defamatory, injurious or libellous statements, videos or other materials against Akpor. It also awarded N1 million as costs of the suit. The case arose from a Facebook publication made on July 20, 2022, with the caption, “Warri Pastor Kpuf 2Keke passenger”, which the court found to be false and defamatory. Reacting to the judgment, counsel to the cleric, Austin Nyekigbe, a human rights activist, described the ruling as a significant statement on responsible social media engagement. He said the judgment reinforced the principle that freedom to use social media did not confer the right to publish false and defamatory information about others. “People must learn to verify information before rushing to publish it, particularly on social media. An injustice to one is an injustice to all,” he said. Also commenting on the judgment, a Warri-based lawyer, Mrs Eloho Avwaruroro-Okoye, who was present in court, said the decision underscored the legal consequences of irresponsible online publications. According to her, freedom of expression comes with responsibility, adding that those who publish false and damaging information must be prepared to face the legal consequences. She congratulated Akpor on his victory and commended Nyekigbe for his diligence in handling the case. The legal dispute followed allegations linking Akpor and two policemen attached to him to the July 12, 2022, killing of two persons at Ugbolokposo community in Effurun. However, Nyekigbe said police investigations subsequently exonerated his client and the two officers, identified as ASP Mesoro Victor and Inspector Ignatius Achazie. He said findings from the investigation, including witness statements, vehicle identification exercises and church CCTV footage, contradicted allegations linking the cleric to the killings. According to him, the police investigation report established that Akpor was at his church when the incident occurred, concluding that he was “going on with his religious business in the Church”. nigeria.title: Troops neutralise suspected criminal, arrest five in Plateau
nigeria.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Troops of Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP) have neutralised a suspected notorious criminal in Wase Local Government Area and arrested five suspected phone snatchers during a raid on a hotel in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The operations also led to the recovery of 26 mobile phones and other items suspected to be stolen, including laptops, earpods and power banks. Military sources disclosed that the suspected criminal, identified as Abubakar Ango, was arrested on November 4 by troops of Sector 2 OPEP at Kukawa village in Wase. “At about 7:20 a.m. on November 6, during interrogation, the suspect reportedly confessed to involvement in several criminal activities and agreed to lead troops to his gang’s hideouts in a village forest,” the sources said. They explained that the mission was intended to facilitate the recovery of weapons and possible arrest of other members of the gang. “However, while being escorted to the location, the suspect allegedly attempted to seize the rifle of one of the soldiers, prompting an immediate response that resulted in his neutralisation,” they said. On the Jos operation, the sources said troops of Sector 1 OPEP arrested five suspected criminals during a raid on a Hotel along Baring Road in Jos North. “The troops, while on patrol, responded to a report of phone snatching at about 9 p.m. on November 6, 2026. They disclosed that the five suspects were found in possession of the tracked phone, while a further search led to the recovery of 26 mobile phones, 27 pouches, three MP devices, two earpods, an HP laptop, a knife and four power banks. “The vehicle belonging to the suspects was also towed to the headquarters of Sector 1 for a comprehensive search,” the sources added. “The suspects and recovered exhibits have been taken into custody for further investigation and necessary action,” the sources said. nigeria.title: Man returns home after 28-yr journey walking around the world
nigeria.description: A British adventurer, Karl Bushby, has returned to his childhood home in Hull, northern England, after completing a 28-year walking journey around the world that covered approximately 50,000 kilometres. Bushby, 57, was welcomed by his mother, Angela, outside her terraced house on Monday, November 2, 2026, beneath a banner reading “Welcome Home Son”. Hundreds of supporters had gathered in the city centre to celebrate his return before he completed the final stretch of his journey to his mother’s home. “Sorry to keep you waiting,” he joked to the cheering crowd. “Is that it, is it done?” Bushby began the expedition, known as the Goliath Expedition, in November 1998 in Punta Arenas, southern Chile. His goal was to travel around the world and return to his hometown without using any form of motorised transport to advance his journey. Carrying a tent, a few hundred dollars and a plastic camera, he initially expected the expedition to take about 12 years. His route took him north through the Americas before crossing the frozen Bering Strait from Alaska into Russia. He subsequently travelled through Mongolia and China, swam across the Caspian Sea and continued towards Europe. The journey also involved navigating the dense Darien Gap jungle between Colombia and Panama, crossing international borders and dealing with visa restrictions. Bushby was detained after entering Russia, while funding difficulties and the global financial crisis of 2008, which cost him major sponsors, contributed to delays that extended the expedition to 28 years. In the final stages of the journey, he swam across the English Channel last month, clearing one of the remaining major obstacles before walking the final distance to Hull. Speaking after his arrival, Bushby acknowledged the support he received from people and organisations across different countries. “They say it takes a village, but literally it took a world to get me here,” he said. “The kindness of strangers, so many, from individuals to nation-states, to get me back here today. I didn’t do this alone. There was a big team. The biggest team. Earth.” A feature-length documentary about his expedition is currently in production, while Bushby is expected to begin a speaking tour across England in the coming weeks. nigeria.title: BEDC announces salary increase for staff
nigeria.description: Benin Electricity Distribution Company (BEDC) Plc has announced salary increases for all staff following an agreement with two recognised labour unions, effective Dec. 1. This is contained in a statement issued by the management of the electricity distribution firm on Sunday in Benin. SSAEAC was represented by its Deputy General Secretary, Comrade Innocent Lord-Douglas, while NUEE was represented by Comrade Mbang Ntukubes. Lawani expressed regret that the industrial action occurred before the agreed date for concluding negotiations, as reaffirmed at the Oct. 7 meeting. He also explained that BEDC’s approved operational expenditure framework had remained fundamentally unchanged since 2013, in spite of rising costs and prevailing economic realities. According to him, access to the company’s full approved operational expenditure allocation depends on meeting prescribed collection performance thresholds, while shortfalls result in reduced allocations. BEDC commended the leadership of NUEE and SSAEAC for their cooperation and constructive engagement in reaching an amicable resolution. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. sports.title: Jemimah Rodrigues to lead Mumbai in Super League stage of Senior Women's T20 Trophy
sports.description: MUMBAI : India women's team batter Jemimah Rodrigues will lead Mumbai in the upcoming Super League stage of the Senior Women's T20 Trophy. The Super League will be played in Ahmedabad from November 14. Rodrigues had smashed 107 off just 47 balls against Pondicherry in their sixth and last match of the league stage of the Senior Women's T20 in Pune on Friday to star in Mumbai's 83-run victory. Rodrigues' century took Mumbai to the Super League stage of the tournament. Returning from a four-month layoff from the game due to a hamstring injury, Rodrigues had scored 58 off 41 balls against Delhi and 26 not out off 19 balls against Uttar Pradesh in a nine-over game. "Jemi's century yesterday was quite good, because the ball wasn't coming nicely on the bat. There was low bounce, it wasn't a flat pitch, but she placed the ball well, piercing the gap between two fielders, instead of trying to hit the ball hard. She played very smartly; it was a smartly built innings, as, realising the nature of the wicket, she didn't want to go for big shots. She came to bat in the fifth over of the innings and started off with two paddle sweeps, which got her two twos, and then gave us the necessary momentum. She paced her knock well and got to her century in the last over," Mumbai Women's team head coach Ajay Kadam told TOI. Interestingly, despite being the Delhi Capitals captain, Rodrigues wasn't the Mumbai skipper in the league stage of the tournament, as she joined the team late. Mumbai were captained by Manali Dakshini. "Jemimah was fine with that. She has no issues with that. She's a team player," Kadam said. Praising the impact of Rodrigues on the team, Kadam said, "Jemimah has definitely added a lot of energy to our dressing room. She has gained vast experience by now. Her presence matters a lot. The girls look up to her. She joined the team after a few matches, but since then, has played her role very well. She has lifted the team to a whole new level, given them confidence. She is a star."

sports.title: Superstitions prevail: If it ain’t broke, don’t move
sports.description: As Erick Fedde and Kyle Teel celebrated the White Sox clinching the AL Wild Card series, fans could take a breath and relax following a day of superstitious rituals. | (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) I didn’t move. Not when Sam Antonacci doubled to open the second game of the American League Wild Card series against the Houston Astros. Not when Kyle Teel singled him home. And certainly not when Andrew Benintendi delivered a two-run single that helped the Chicago White Sox build a four-run lead before the Astros could record their second out. There I sat, practically frozen in place, convinced that the slightest movement might somehow bring Chicago’s offensive outburst to an abrupt end. Never mind that I was hundreds of miles from Daikin Park in Houston. Never mind that the White Sox players had absolutely no idea who I was, what I was wearing or whether I had gotten up to use the bathroom. And never mind that my position on the couch had precisely zero influence on a baseball traveling toward home plate at nearly 100 mph. The White Sox were scoring. I wasn’t moving. It wasn’t until Tristan Peters singled home Chicago’s fourth run and the inning finally ended that I allowed myself to get comfortable again. Welcome to the wonderfully irrational world of sports superstitions, where otherwise reasonable adults become convinced that a lucky jersey, a particular snack or the precise arrangement of living room furniture might determine whether their favorite team wins or loses. And apparently, I’m not alone. A little luck never hurt anyone My postseason wardrobe consisted of White Sox jerseys. Every game. No exceptions. When football season arrives, the situation becomes considerably more complicated. I pay attention to whether my team (either the Chicago Bears or Jacksonville Jaguars) is playing at home or on the road, choosing my jersey accordingly. I try to eat the same foods, snack at the same times and sit in the same location. It’s definitely easy for my wife. Honestly, she probably thinks it’s a little obnoxious. Sometimes a particular shirt becomes lucky. Other times, a hat gets blamed for a loss. I understand how ridiculous this sounds. I also know that if the White Sox had continued scoring every time I remained motionless during the playoffs, there’s a good chance someone would have needed to bring me dinner. But the impulse to create rituals around sporting events isn’t unusual. A 2018 study published in Sport Management Review examined how superstitions influence the experience of watching sports. Researchers found that these behaviors were associated with fans’ emotional states during games and that more superstitious fans were more likely to attribute outcomes to outside influences such as fate or officiating. In other words, fans aren’t necessarily trying to control a baseball game. They’re trying to control how helpless they feel while watching one. sports.title: Previous Infantino ally Wenger considering FIFA presidency bid
sports.description: FILE PHOTO - FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development Arsène Wenger stands in the stadium prior to the start of the UEFA Champions League final soccer match between Borussia Dortmund and Real Madrid at Wembley Stadium. (is associated with: «Previous Infantino ally Wenger considering FIFA presidency bid») Robert Michael/dpa Arsène Wenger is considering whether to put himself forward as a candidate for the FIFA presidency, the Press Association understands. The former Arsenal manager, 77, remains in the mix as one of a number of candidates UEFA could give its backing to as it seeks to put up a credible alternative to incumbent Gianni Infantino. However, Wenger is not yet seen as the preferred candidate, with others still being evaluated as well. It is understood he is still undecided over whether to run. Wenger’s reputation within football and close knowledge of the FIFA administration would make him a formidable opponent for Infantino if he did choose to go for it, with the Frenchman having served as FIFA’s chief of global football development since 2019. UEFA is expected to hold meetings of its executive committee as well as gather together its member national associations this coming week to hold further discussions on who should get Europe’s support. Infantino’s position appeared under threat when his plans to sell a minority stake in a World Cup company, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), to private investors came to light. The plan was rejected by three continental confederations, including UEFA, and even though Infantino later abandoned it, the European body said it had “lost confidence” in the Swiss and has since been working to identify someone to run against him. Wenger spoke out about the FFE plan on August 4, saying he was “not involved” in it and first became aware of it through media reports. He added: “The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent FIFA that serves our game with commitment, transparency, and integrity.” Kozo Tashima, the honorary president of the Japanese Football Association (JFA), announced on Thursday he would run for the presidency. Infantino has recovered and has rallied support from Africa, Asia, Oceania and South America. On Friday, he also received the backing of the member nations of the Caribbean Football Union (CFU). The election for the next FIFA president will take place at the FIFA Congress in Rabat, Morocco on March 18 next year.

sports.description: (Photo by N. Hermann/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images Jamal Musiala’s recovery from a muscular injury has taken longer than many expected, which can happen with injuries of that type. However, in an interview with BR24 via t-online (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ), Uli Hoeneß has offered a sobering assessment of the Bayern Munich star’s overall situation, including hi s neurological condition. The club’s honorary president spoke about Musiala’s condition, revealin g that the 23-year-old is dealing with a condition that cannot simply be cured and raising doubts about whether he will ever return to his previous level of performance. Hoeneß made a point of distinguishing Musiala’s situation from Vincent Kom pany’s recent health problems, suggesting that Bayern Munich is facing a much more complicated dilemma with its young playmaker. “With Musiala, the situation is completely different [to Vincent Kompany]. We’re in a dilemma there. He has an illness that cannot s imply be cured, but can be managed to some extent with medication,” Hoeneß stated. Hoeneß then left the doo r open to an uncomfortable possibility: Musiala might never completely recover his previous level of performance. “Whether he will ever regain the level of performance he once had…” The Bayern Munich legend also addressed the contractual and financial complications surrounding the situation, explaining that Musiala’ s condition was not covered by the insurance provisions in his contract. He expanded on the difficu lt position this creates for the club: “We’re in a dilemma with him. He has an illness that cannot simply be cured, bu t can be managed to some extent with medication. However, whether he will ever regain the level of performance he once had remains uncertain. He is still receiving his salary, of course. But just imagine if FC Bayern were now to question his contract and say: ‘W hat he is capable of delivering now is no longer what was stipulated in the contract.'” There is a lot to un pack here. Musiala remains one of Bayern Munich’s most important players, and the club obviously has a responsibility to supp ort him through this difficult period. He flew a little too close to the sun though, injuring his shoulder while doing the worm ( seriously ) and then getting smashed by Corey Anderson in a would-be title eliminator. For years afterward, Walker struggled to find consistency or build momentum. By 2022, a Light Heavyweight title shot was out of reach, and I advocated for Walker to move up to Heavyweight . technology.title: Physicists listened to electrical noise to crack a superconductor mystery
technology.description: Superconductors carry electricity without resistance, but most only work a few degrees above absolute zero. In the late 1980s, copper-based materials called cuprates were found to superconduct at higher temperatures—reachable with affordable liquid nitrogen. Yet nearly 40 years later, physicists still don't agree on why. In a recent Science study, a team of physicists led by Milan Allan of Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and Ingmar Swart of Utrecht University in the Netherlands has found some answers by listening to the faint electrical crackle of current flowing into a cuprate. The missing electrons Central to the mystery of cuprates’ high-temperature superconductivity is a strange state called the pseudogap. “The pseudogap is a phenomenon of missing electrons,” Allan said. Above the temperature at which cuprates become superconducting, some of their electrons seem to vanish—measurements find far fewer of them at the energies where they should be. “Everybody knows that from different probes, you see that there's these vanishing electrons, but nobody knows why,” Allan said. technology.title: Doom delivers five minutes of terminal violence on an IBM mainframe
technology.description: Can an IBM Z mainframe run Doom? Of course it can. The more interesting question is whether you can play it through a text terminal without ruining your eyesight. WND Software's browser demo connects to an IBM Z mainframe over SSH using its terminal emulator. Wojciech Graj's DOOM-ASCII supplies the text-based carnage, replacing conventional graphics with colored characters. There's no sound. It is, however, completely playable (although you might need to recalibrate your vision to work out what is going on, particularly with regard to distant objects). Sessions are limited to five minutes, with room for up to 50 simultaneous users, but we had no trouble getting in. ASCII also presented no issues once the game was in motion. This writer played the original shareware release on an Amstrad ALT386SX portable, so squinting at an indistinct demon felt reassuringly familiar. That Doom can be persuaded to run on an IBM Z mainframe is not particularly noteworthy. The code has turned up everywhere from databases to PCB designers . Even the humble Pi Pico was roped into the fun. Keeping the action playable through a text terminal is the more entertaining achievement. A year ago, an IBM consultant persuaded Doom to run on IBM Z and LinuxONE using VNC to bring the pixelated mayhem to life. Using a terminal emulator, while a neat demonstration of the capabilities of WND's software, is perhaps more an example of "because I can" masochism. It's undeniably an enjoyable way to burn through five minutes. No installation or login required – just a willingness to shoot at punctuation. ®

technology.title: Internet governance about to get its quadrennial stress test at ITU meeting
technology.description: The International Telecommunications Union (ITU) kicks off its quadrennial plenipotentiary on Monday, and internet governance organizations are bracing in case the event becomes a forum for nation-states to try to challenge their roles. The ITU is the United Nations' specialized agency for information and communication technologies, meaning its members are nation-states. The body's role is to facilitate international connectivity, which it does by managing radio spectrum, satellite orbits, and working on relevant technical standards. Its key standards are pervasive. ITU-T X.509 sets out the rules of public key infrastructure. ITU-T E.164 governs telephone numbers. ITU-T H.264 and 265 define the video codecs used for most online streams. The ITU's role is largely uncontested, yet its work gets very close to that of the organizations who work on technologies that make the internet work. Those bodies include the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF); the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN), which oversees the domain name system; and the regional internet registries (RIRs), which manage IP addresses. The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) works on HTML, CSS, and accessibility. Governments participate in work at those internet governance bodies but are just one voice among many and can't override the consensus-driven decision-making process they use, under a system which has come to be known as the multi-stakeholder governance model. At a 2025 event called WSIS+20, the United Nations endorsed multi-stakeholder governance by deciding that its Internet Governance Forum (IGF) should become a permanent body. That decision effectively endorsed multi-stakeholder governance, and kept the ITU out of internet standards. Yet the IGF hasn't met since WSIS+20, so it is yet to start operating meaningfully as a permanent body. This year's ITU meeting is therefore a moment at which stakeholders can stress-test the delicate balance between the ITU, internet governance bodies, and the emerging IGF. Such a test could see ITU members try to have it pursue new fields that overlap with work performed by internet governance organizations. This has already happened before. China tried to have the ITU work on " New IP" – a major revision to internet protocol, a technology the IETF manages. In 2022, Russia and China backed a candidate for the ITU presidency who favored giving nations a stronger role in internet governance, potentialy by having the ITU take over some standards work. That candidate was not elected. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 8, 2005: Europe launches Venus Express, its first mission to Venus
science.description: null On Nov. 8, 2005, Europe launched its first mission to Venus. The spacecraft was called Venus Express. Venus is a hothouse planet, one where the atmospheric pressure can easily crush an unprotected spacecraft. Even from orbit, Venus Express had to survive harsh radiation. But the spacecraft lasted for more than nine years. During that time, Venus Express saw a weird vortex swirling around Venus's south pole . It also saw possible signs of active volcanoes . Venus Express also discovered that the planet generates its own auroras . These auroras happen when particles from the sun hit charged particles in the atmosphere. Late in the Venus Express mission, controllers told the spacecraft to dip down into Venus's clouds — even though the spacecraft wasn't designed to do this. It performed well, but eventually it stopped listening to commands. The spacecraft burned up in the atmosphere in January 2015. A Russian Soyuz rocket launches the Venus Express spacecraft to Venus on Nov. 8, 2005.. (Image credit: ESA) Why it mattered Venus Express established ESA as the third world organization to successfully send a probe to study Venus, following the United States and Soviet Union. (Japan's JAXA became the fourth five years later.) "By studying Venus, scientists learn how Earth-like planets change over time," reads a summary of the planet's exploration prepared by The Planetary Society. "Orbital studies [like Venus Express] hint that Venus may have hosted habitable oceans before becoming inhospitable." "By studying Venus, we can learn how Earth-like planets evolve and what shapes planets throughout the galaxy into temperate, lush worlds instead of sweltering hothouses. Venus also helps scientists model Earth’s climate, and may serve as a cautionary tale on how dramatically a planet’s climate can change," wrote the Society. An illustration of the Venus Express spacecraft in orbit around Venus. (Image credit: ESA) ESA returned to Venus in 2018 when BepiColombo, its joint mission with JAXA, used the planet's gravity to redirect its path toward the planet Mercury. Want more space history? science.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
science.description: A new computer simulation that depicts Earth, or a rocky planet in general, without life is the latest tool in the quest to discover whether or not we are alone in the universe. Life leaves its mark on a planet, particularly its atmosphere, in the form of a mixture of biochemically created gases. Some are obvious, while others can be produced by both biology and geology, meaning that distinguishing a planet that has life from one that does not, solely based on what gases we can detect in its atmosphere, can be difficult. The key is in knowing which atmospheric conditions can be explained without life. To aid in distinguishing between habitable and inhabited planets, planetary scientist Samantha Gilbert-Janizek of the University of California, Riverside, developed a model that simulates the evolution of a rocky planet without life. "The model can help us see how habitable but non-living planets might mimic living planets," Gilbert-Janizek, who was a PhD student at the University of Washington when the research was conducted, said in a statement. Gilbert-Janizek built upon a model previously developed by Washington’s Rory Barnes that simulated the core, mantle, and crust of a planet. This new model pushed the simulation two steps further by incorporating the surface and atmosphere of the planet as well. In all, the model simulates 19 properties of a rocky planet that are not related to life, including the amount of heat a planet receives from its star , the exchange of heat and chemicals from the core to the surface, and the outflow of certain gases from the subsurface. Gilbert-Janizek’s starting point was to simulate the development of Earth had life never arisen here, therefore providing a baseline with which to compare to exoplanets . She ran the simulation from the birth of Earth 4.5 billion years ago to 500 million years into the future. The result was a lifeless world, but one that still had oceans and an atmosphere. "When we interpret observations of an exoplanet’s atmosphere, this tool will help us determine the probability that what we observe indicates life on the surface," said Gilbert-Janizek. An illustration shows the landscape of a primordial Earth before life arose as lightning splits the skies (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) What makes the simulation especially useful is its plug-and-play nature. Researchers can simply apply the bulk properties of whichever planet they are studying to the model, and then just let it run. If the result is a planet with an atmosphere that matches what is detected spectroscopically by the James Webb Space Telescope or, in the future, the various extremely large 30-meter-plus ground-based telescopes or NASA’s planned Habitable Worlds Observatory , then we know that planet probably does not have life as we know it. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments." Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences. It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. science.description: null NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition. "I feel good. "It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites for the USSF's Space Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST) portfolio based on SpaceX's Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches," NextSpaceflight.com wrote in a mission description . Starlink is SpaceX's LEO broadband megaconstellation, which consists of more than 11,000 active satellites.
